messages:
incidents-bot: Paging mike (oncall) for incident — latency spike affecting streaming responses (p95/p99 breach) :rotating_light:

mike (oncall): on it. can someone post current numbers and which region?

sophia (sre): seeing p95 jump from 180ms -> 1.2s and p99 ~ 3.6s for /v1/chat/stream in eu-west-1. error-rate low but streaming stalls up (clients reporting long pauses).

raj (mlinfra): correlating with heavy JSON-mode tool-schema render jobs. CPU on preproc workers jumped to 95% and tokenization latency tail increased.

jordan (runtime): confirmed — queue depth on preproc-pool peaked, and we hit continuous-batching fallback which increases head latency.

mike (oncall): customer-impact? any degraded SRs?

cs-rep: small set of premium customers in EU reported broken live streams and timeouts. One support ticket elevated. No mass outages yet but SLAs at risk if sustained.

raj (mlinfra): quick probe: top-k preproc types by CPU:
```
$ kubectl top pods -n prod | grep preproc
preproc-0    890m  1.1Gi
preproc-1    920m  1.2Gi
preproc-2    870m  1.0Gi
```
logs show repeated expensive path from prompt-template renderer when tool schema contains large arrays:
```
[WARN] template_render: expanding tool schema array size=1200, time=312ms
[INFO] tokenizer: token_count=4800 prompt_construct_ms=615
[ERROR] stream_sink: stall detected, gap_ms=2200
```

sophia (sre): streaming stalls seem tied to prompt construction + tokenizer expansion. tail tokens spike when JSON-mode validate+pretty-print runs on large tool schema fields.

jordan (runtime): timeline: spike started ~+2m after automated rollout of template-opt branch (rolled this morning). possibly changed rendering to run full validation for JSON-mode.

tess (prod-eng): that's the PR I landed for strict schema checks. it adds a pretty-print pass. I can revert if needed.

mike (oncall): immediate mitigations we can do now? things to avoid customer impact while we triage.

raj (mlinfra): short list: 1) disable JSON-mode pretty-print globally (cheap config flip) 2) route new streaming traffic to lower-cost fallback model variant (less token-heavy templates) 3) increase preproc pool autoscale threshold or add short-term burst machines 4) apply per-request schema size cap at proxy (reject huge tool arrays)

sophia (sre): doing 1 now — flipping feature-flag `json_pretty_print` -> false in prod. will monitor.

incidents-bot: Feature flag json_pretty_print toggled to false by sophia (sre) at root:prod (audit id 0x9f3b)

raj (mlinfra): adding 2) routing tweak — bump traffic weight to model-variant lightweight-v1 for canary 10% -> 40% for eu-west-1 for 10m. issuing rollout.

jordan (runtime): rolling route now.

mike (oncall): runbooks / checks please. I want p95/p99 baseline and streaming stall count before/after flip.

sophia (sre): baseline (pre-flip): p95 1.22s, p99 3.6s, streaming-stalls 47/min across eu-west-1.

sophia (sre): post-flip (5m): p95 320ms, p99 900ms, streaming-stalls 8/min. initial improvement promising.

tess (prod-eng): re: revert — I can roll back the pretty-print commit if toggling doesn't fully mitigate. but prefer to keep for correctness once we redesign to stream-validate rather than blocking validate.

raj (mlinfra): also added short-term autoscale: spin 2 extra preproc pods (scaled up).

incidents-bot: Scale event: preproc ASG +2 pods (requested by raj (mlinfra))

jordan (runtime): note — we saw increased connection churn after routing bump; reducing per-connection chunk size on streaming from 4k -> 1k bytes improves backpressure handling. deploying config change.

mike (oncall): good. any risk to other regions?

sophia (sre): no, this was concentrated on eu-west-1 because heavy template traffic there and the rollout affected that pool only. global metrics flat.

cs-rep: sent a short status note to impacted customers: "We observed increased stalls; we've applied mitigations and expect recovery. We'll follow up with root cause and timeline."

mike (oncall): action items:
- tess: prepare rollback PR for pretty-print (if needed) and a follow-up to change validate->stream-validate (ETA 24h)
- raj: keep autoscale until steady for 30m, add temporary request-size cap at proxy cfg (200KB)
- jordan: monitor streaming chunk change, confirm no regressions in memory/throughput
- sophia: keep p95/p99 charting and collect sample traces for tail requests (+include prompt payloads)
- cs-rep: update customers in 30m or when stable

tess (prod-eng): ack, starting rollback PR draft and a design note for streaming validation.

raj (mlinfra): added quick blocking rule at edge to reject requests with tool schema array length > 1000 with 413 for now.

sophia (sre): collecting traces: attaching example trace id x-trace-9ab4 with heavy prompt payload. sample shows prompt_construct_ms=640 and tokenizer tail 2200ms.

mike (oncall): status check in 15.

incidents-bot: automatic severity suggestion = sev2 (potential SLA breach). oncall to confirm.

mike (oncall): marking sev2. will keep the channel open.

--- 15 minutes later ---

sophia (sre): update: p95 280ms, p99 650ms, stalls 3/min. preproc CPU normalized to ~55%.

jordan (runtime): streaming chunk size change did not increase errors. throughput stable.

mike (oncall): seems resolved for now. moving to mitigation->postmortem.

tess (prod-eng): will revert pretty-print in next 30m and open postmortem doc that captures why full-validate was run inline.

raj (mlinfra): follow-up: add a lightweight token-estimation pass before heavy render to short-circuit huge templates. will draft an RFC.

cs-rep: final customer note posted. one customer wants timeline + rollback details — will coordinate with eng for wording.

mike (oncall): closing incident channel in 30m unless regressions. thanks all. :raised_hands:

incidents-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED: severity downgraded to monitor. closed by mike (oncall)
